newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian court dismisses Shell complaint.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian court dismisses Shell complaint.

text.p: Slovenia's Constitutional Court on Wednesday dismissed a request by Royal Dutch/Shell unit Shell Slovenia to lift the country's strict limitations on the ownership of motorway petrol stations.

The Slovenian government called for bids to operate petrol stations along some 500 km (300 miles) of motorways to be constructed in the country by the year 2004, but placed severe restrictions on potential bidders.
In a decree, the government required companies wanting to operate motorway stations already to own three petrol stations elsewhere in the country as well as to operate a supply depot within Slovenia.
Shell, which currently owns no petrol stations in Slovenia, claimed the provision was unconstitutional and in violation of the principles of free competition.

But the court said it was unable to lift the restrictions because to do so would hold up the government's ambitious motorway construction programme. "That would hold up the whole project," it said in its ruling.
Roy Willye, chief executive of Shell Slovenia told Reuters the company had no immediate comment to make.

The company previously has said it has no plans to build a supply depot in Slovenia because it was not cost-effective. Shell already operates two supply depots in neighbouring Austria and Italy, both located some 50 km (30 miles) across the Slovenian border.
